official.deadline_central_display: 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time) - deadline for applicants and referees, 2026 cycle (closed)
official.deadline_note: The 2026 call opened on 15 October 2025 and closed for applicants and referees on 31 January 2026 Beijing Time. The 2027 call had not been published on the UCAS site as at 10 October 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2026 intake (call opened 15 October 2025; 2027 cycle not yet published)
official.status_note: The 2026 round closed for applicants and referees on 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time) and UCAS has published the results announcement for the 2026 CAS-ANSO Scholarship; the published page remains the 2026 call and no 2027 call was posted as at 10 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The published coverage table lists a tuition waiver for both the master's and PhD programmes; the 2026 UCAS admission call confirms students awarded the CAS-ANSO Scholarship are exempt from tuition fees.
benefits: Full tuition waiver for both the PhD and Master's programmes
Monthly stipend of CNY 6,000 or 7,000 for PhD candidates depending on whether the qualification test has been passed, of which CNY 1,000 is provided by the CAS Institute
Monthly stipend of CNY 3,000 for master's candidates
Application fee waiver (CAS-ANSO applicants are not required to pay the RMB 600 application fee)
One international travel allowance from the awardee's home country to China
eligibility: Does not hold Chinese citizenship and holds a valid foreign passport
Friendly to China and abiding by Chinese laws and decrees and UCAS rules and regulations
Meets the admission criteria for international students of UCAS for the 2026 programmes
Not currently pursuing a master's degree at any university/institution in China (master's applicants) or a doctoral degree (PhD applicants)
Does not take up other assignments during the scholarship period
Is not applying for the CAS-ANSO Scholarship through both USTC and UCAS simultaneously
requirements: Meet the admission criteria for international students of UCAS (degree equivalent to a Chinese bachelor's for master's, a Chinese master's for doctoral)

English proficiency required: a valid IELTS or TOEFL result or other proof of English proficiency (not necessary for native English speakers); HSK level 5 with at least 180 for Chinese-instructed programmes
Select 'the CAS-ANSO Scholarship' in the UCAS online application
Tick the additional box if consideration as an ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship candidate is wanted
Submit the file and application in the UCAS Online Admission System before the deadline - the deadline applies to both applicants and referees
documents: Scanned copy of the passport information page (ordinary passport, at least 1 year validity)
Two-inch recent bareheaded photo matching the passport photo
Complete CV with detailed education and research experiences from university onwards
Scanned copies of original degree certificates (bachelor's for master's applicants; master's and bachelor's for doctoral applicants) or a pre-graduation certificate
Scanned copies of complete original academic transcripts
Scanned copy of a valid IELTS or TOEFL result or other proof of English proficiency
First page and abstract of up to 5 representative published academic papers, if available
Motivation letter covering purpose of study, academic background, reasons for applying, study plan and career goals
Two reference letters from professors or associate professors who are not the prospective UCAS supervisor, on institutional letterhead with signature and date
Supervisor's Acceptance Form, if a supervisor has already accepted the applicant
selection_criteria: Merit-based selection combining review of application documents with an entrance examination, mainly an interview, set by the UCAS school or CAS institute

For the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO sub-category, TWAS/UNESCO selects up to 40 PhD students from developing countries each year, with 10 prioritised for climate-related research and special (non-exclusive) consideration for Least Developed Countries and women
Awardees must pass annual assessments; failure can lead to termination of the scholarship, discontinuity of study, or being issued only a certificate of attendance rather than a formal degree
coverage: Tuition waiver for both the PhD programme and the Master's programme
PhD monthly stipend of CNY 6,000 or 7,000 depending on whether the qualification test has been passed, of which CNY 1,000 is provided by the CAS Institute
One international travel allowance from the awardee's home country to China, one trip per awarded candidate
application_method: Apply through the UCAS Online Admission System for International Students at https://is.ucas.ac.cn/#/login
Choose 'the CAS-ANSO Scholarship' in the application form
Tick the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship box if relevant
File and submit the application in the system before the deadline; referees must also submit by the same date
Prepare the application materials listed in the Call for 2026 Master's/Doctoral Degree Programs for International Students
official.application_route: Single online route: file the UCAS Online Admission System application, select the CAS-ANSO Scholarship inside it, and submit before the deadline together with referee letters.
official.study_mode: Full-time postgraduate degree study (master's or PhD) at UCAS or CAS institutes, including centralized training in Chinese language and culture
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must not hold Chinese citizenship and must hold a valid foreign passport; applicants already in China at the time of application are not eligible for the travel subsidy
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship supports 100 to 200 master's and 300 PhD students every year from all over the world at USTC, UCAS and CAS institutes
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction; the degree programme must meet UCAS admission criteria for international students. Applicants may not apply through both USTC and UCAS simultaneously.
official.research_requirement: Degree study includes practical research and completion of a degree thesis at UCAS colleges and schools or CAS institutes; awardees must not take up other assignments during the scholarship period
official.duration: The basic study period is commonly 3 years for master's degree students and 3-4 years for doctoral students per the 2026 UCAS admission call; the scholarship duration itself is stated explicitly in the Admission Notice.
official.description: The CAS-ANSO Scholarship (Degree Program), previously the ANSO Scholarship for Young Talents, is the postgraduate scholarship of the Alliance of National and International Science Organizations for the Belt and Road Regions (ANSO), sponsored by the Chinese Academy of Sciences and administered at UCAS for master's and PhD study. It supports 100 to 200 master's students and 300 PhD students every year, and includes the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship sub-category selecting up to 40 PhD students from developing countries annually.
official.program_type: Postgraduate degree scholarship of ANSO, sponsored by the Chinese Academy of Sciences and administered by UCAS
official.english_requirement: Proficient in English or Chinese. The 2026 UCAS admission call requires a valid IELTS or TOEFL result or other proof of English proficiency (not necessary for applicants whose mother tongue is English); applicants for Chinese-instructed programmes must hold HSK level 5 with at least 180.

The scholarship call page was verified for eligibility, the 15 October 2025 opening, the 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time) deadline for applicants and referees, the application portal and the CAS-ANSO/TWAS box; the 2026 admission call page was verified for the full application-materials list, English/HSK proficiency requirements, study periods, and the exemption of CAS-ANSO awardees from tuition and the application fee. applicant_utility.summary: This is a single-window online application: you file once in the UCAS Online Admission System, tick the CAS-ANSO Scholarship box inside the application, and both your referees and you must beat the same deadline - in the 2026 round that was 31 January Beijing Time, so referee letters submitted a day late were fatal. The stipend differs sharply by level (CNY 3,000 per month for master's versus CNY 6,000-7,000 for doctoral candidates), and the PhD figure only rises to 7,000 after you pass the qualification test, so plan your first-year budget around the lower rate. Age limits are hard cut-offs (born after 1 January 1996 for master's, 1 January 1991 for PhD), and applying simultaneously through USTC and UCAS is an automatic disqualification.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Young non-Chinese nationals (under roughly 30 for master's, 35 for PhD) with a bachelor's or master's degree, English or Chinese proficiency, and a research plan that fits a UCAS or CAS institute supervisor.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the birth-date cut-offs for your level before anything else (after 1 January 1996 master's; after 1 January 1991 PhD)
Line up two professor-level referees who are not your prospective UCAS supervisor and give them the deadline in advance
Prepare the full document set: passport, degree certificates, transcripts, English certificate, CV, motivation letter, up to 5 published papers
Choose either USTC or UCAS - never both - and decide early whether to tick the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO box
Contact a potential supervisor first: the Supervisor's Acceptance Form strengthens the file, though it is not mandatory
common_rejection_risks: Referee letters arriving after the applicant deadline - the deadline explicitly covers referees too
Being currently enrolled in a master's or doctoral programme anywhere in China, which disqualifies you at that level and is reported to your current institution
Applying through both USTC and UCAS, which is an automatic disqualification
Missing the age cut-off for the level applied for
Failing the annual assessment after award, which can terminate the scholarship and leave you with only a certificate of attendance rather than a degree
Submitting duplicate accounts or multiple applications, which UCAS checks for and disqualifies
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond the waived tuition, monthly stipend, insurance, application fee, one flight and the visa allowance, the UCAS fee schedule puts accommodation (RMB 30 per day shared, RMB 60 single), meals, experiments, meetings and training beyond the curriculum, and any further travel at the student's own expense.
document_audit: All certificates must be in English or Chinese, otherwise the original and a translation must be combined into one PDF - colour scans are required
Expected graduates must upload a pre-graduation certificate and then the final degree certificate and transcripts through the host college before registration
Reference letters must be on the referee's institutional letterhead with signature and date, and the referee cannot be your prospective supervisor
Only up to 5 published papers may be submitted, and unpublished work must not be included
alerts: Applicants already in China when applying receive no travel subsidy
The award binds you to centralized training in Chinese language and culture plus all required credits before thesis work at UCAS or a CAS institute
Work produced during the funding period must be credited to your institute/school and UCAS and must acknowledge the CAS-ANSO Scholarship
The 2026 round is closed and results announced; the next call typically follows the same autumn opening, so watch the UCAS financial aid page from October onwards
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File the UCAS Online Admission System application with the CAS-ANSO Scholarship selected, upload the material set, ensure referees submit by the same deadline, then await document review and an interview-based entrance examination run by the UCAS school or CAS institute.
